claim: CategoryRepository.delete() is dead code and should be removed
rationale: Not dead: it is directly exercised by tests/features/categories/test_categories.py (test at ~line 94) and kept for API symmetry with the other repos. CategoryService.delete_category deliberately bypasses it with an inline commit-free DELETE because repo.delete() commits, which would end the service-owned transaction early and break the INV-7 delete-cascade atomicity (pinned by the INV-7 rollback test). The method is intentional, tested, and must not be removed. Two independent review lanes flagged it as 'dead in the service layer'; that is accurate but the 'remove it' conclusion is wrong.

rationale: All five cited files exist on disk in the same directory as the spec that cites them: tests/features/dashboard/test_min_size.py, tests/features/forecast/{test_forecast_service.py,test_importer_capture.py,test_preview_threading.py}, tests/features/spending_alerts/test_alerts_ui.py (verified by `ls` 2026-08-03). claim: bandit B608 "possible SQL injection" x3 in tests (_recovery_helpers.py:299, test_statements.py:1410/1414) and B608 x3 in src (transactions.py:63/80, vault_migration.py:171, backup.py:395)
rationale: No caller value reaches any statement text. transactions.py:63/80 interpolate `coverage`, itself generated SQL whose variable part is `:delN` placeholder NAMES; ids bind as named parameters. vault_migration.py:171 and backup.py:395 interpolate a table name read from sqlite_master, which SQLite cannot bind as a parameter. The test sites interpolate a module-local `cols` constant and table_names(conn). Every src site already carries a documented `# nosec B608`; verified live by `bandit --ignore-nosec -r src`, which reports each one, so none of those directives is inert.

claim: bandit B108 "probable insecure usage of temp file/directory" x4 (test_auto_update.py:411/421/423, test_obs_packaging.py:612)
rationale: None of the four opens, creates or writes a temp path. The auto_update three are `monkeypatch.setenv("LD_LIBRARY_PATH", "/tmp/_MEIabc123")` — a string literal standing in for PyInstaller's _MEI bundle dir, asserted to be DROPPED from the relaunch env. test_obs_packaging.py:612 substitutes "/tmp/curdir" for $(CURDIR) when probing debian/rules command text. bandit matches the literal "/tmp/" prefix and cannot see that no filesystem call follows.

claim: semgrep insecure-file-permissions on paths.py:37 (0o700) and update_installer.py:274 (0o755)
rationale: paths.py:37 is `os.chmod(directory, 0o700)` — owner-only, the MOST restrictive mode, applied deliberately to stop a permissive umask loosening mkdir's mode and leaking vault existence/size/mtime to other local users. The rule fires on the literal without reading the value. update_installer.py:274 is `os.chmod(new_file, 0o755)`, the mandatory AppImage mode (the file is unlaunchable without the execute bit) replacing a $APPIMAGE that was already 0o755; already carries a documented `# nosec B103`.

All three are test-helper signatures defaulting to the module's MASTER_PASSWORD constant so a suite can build and reopen a throwaway vault without restating the literal. No production code path reaches them; the file is under tests/features/ and is imported only by the recovery_key suite.

claim: vulture: 111 of 113 findings are dead names that pytest or Qt consumes by reflection — pytestmark x77, theme_isolation x17, _selftest _check_* x10, conftest fixtures/attributes, main_window._update_check_worker
rationale: pytestmark is a module global pytest reads by name, never by reference. theme_isolation is a fixture PARAMETER requested for its side effect. _selftest.py's _check_* functions are dispatched from a registry table in the same file. conftest.py's _neutralise_category_library is an autouse fixture. main_window.py's _update_check_worker IS read, via getattr in the shutdown loop at main_window.py:1766. conftest.py's _parent_names x2 is deliberately captured-and-ignored so the real constructor's FIBR-0154 kwarg never TypeErrors the stub — the docstring says so. vulture's static reachability cannot see any of these.

claim: typos: 133 of the 135 findings surviving the `mis-` prefix calibration are domain terms, not misspellings
rationale: `unparseable`/`Unparseable` x39 is a valid variant the project uses as a term of art; `PN` x22 is inside "PNG"/"PNGs"; `certifi` x13 is the PyPI package name; `SELEC`/`UPDAT`/`COLUM`/`DELET` x16 are inside pluralised SQL keywords ("SELECTs", "UPDATEs"); `Flate` x5 is PDF FlateDecode; `Nd` x3 is the Unicode general category; `unparented`/`UNPARENTED` x4 is the Qt term used in main_window.py; `Hed` is inside "ATTACHed"; `empted` is inside "pre-empted"; `caf` is `tar caf`; `OT`/`ND`/`Ue`/`IZ` are inside base64 blobs in _selftest.py; `makro` is Makro, a South African retailer, in category_library.json's merchant patterns; `ambiguious` at ROADMAP.md:927 is a VERBATIM quote of CPython's own misspelled DeprecationWarning in _strptime (confirmed in the installed stdlib source) — correcting it would falsify the quote.
